Subject: Scheduling a service refresh for our private deployment

Hi Vanessa,

We need to schedule a service refresh for our Redwood Private deployment running in our VPC. Compliance is requiring a quarterly version review and the security team wants a formal window with an explicit version freeze and rollback criteria documented.

A couple of constraints from our side:
- We can do maintenance windows between 01:00-06:00 PT weekdays or any time on Saturday morning (02:00-09:00 PT).
- We must avoid a >3 hour total outage for the inference endpoints (we can tolerate short rolling restarts).
- Network firewall change windows require 48 hours notice.

Can you propose a timeline, pin strategy (what gets frozen), and quick rollback triggers? Also, if you can attach any runbook/checklist you use for Private upgrades that would help our auditors.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Corp
laura.chen@acmecorp.com

Hi Laura — thanks for the head's up. 

High-level proposal (summary):
- Window options (pick one): Weekday early AM: 02:00–05:00 PT (3 hours), or Saturday: 03:00–07:00 PT (4 hours, staggered).
- Version freeze: pin serving runtime and model family during the window; allow non-serving agent config (logs, metrics) to update post-window. The only allowed image changes during the window are backend-security patches from our distro list (critical CVE fixes) — everything else will be held until the next scheduled refresh.
- Canary/rollout: 10% canary for first 30 minutes, expand to 50% for next 60 minutes, then full traffic if metrics OK.
- Rollback triggers: any 15-min window with error rate >1.5x baseline OR tail latency >2x SLO for two contiguous sampling intervals (5 min each) OR a failed KV cache warmup for >10% of pods.
- Fallbacks: automatic route to hosted Redwood API for critical endpoints if private capacity degrades beyond threshold.

I'll need a rapid engineering review on the network steps (firewall rules, IP/port changes) and the exact toastpoints we use for canary gating. Dev/So must confirm the gating thresholds and the expected time-to-rollback for a full revert.

Attaching a compact runbook and a canary checklist for your auditors. Will follow up with a version freeze manifest.

Can we tentatively aim for Saturday 03:00–07:00 PT next weekend (Oct 9) and I will coordinate notices? If that doesn't work I can propose the weekday 02:00–05:00 PT slot.

Short ask for you: confirm preferred window and whether you require us to schedule the firewall change from our side or if Acme will handle it.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

> - Window options (pick one): Weekday early AM: 02:00–05:00 PT (3 hours), or Saturday: 03:00–07:00 PT (4 hours, staggered).

Thanks Vanessa — quick technical notes and acceptance criteria from infra/runtime: 

Pre-steps (48–72 hours before):
- Bake images and publish immutable tags for runtime and model-serving artifacts. Publish manifest with SHA256 for all pinned components.
- Validate repo hash in Acme's image registry (we will provide the expected digests).
- Health-check baseline run (qps/latency) for the 24h prior to window (capture baseline metrics).

During window:
- Canary nodes are spun in a separate ASG/pool with drain protection disabled for the rollback path. Canary config: 2 pods (10% approx) in first stage, 6 pods (50%) second stage for your fleet size.
- KV warm starts: we will pre-warm the KV cache on canary nodes; if >10% fail to warm within 3 minutes we abort and revert.
- Networking: no port changes expected. If there is a FQDN or internal VIP change, we require a maintenance NAT rule change which must be applied in the first 10 minutes of the window to avoid DNS TTL complications.

Rollback timing expectations:
- Automatic traffic shift back to previous image by disabling the canary route — target 3 minutes to start traffic back, full restoration within 20–30 minutes depending on cache warmup.
- If we need to fail over to hosted Redwood, that path is scripted and can be enacted in ~10–15 minutes (requires an authentication token swap and firewall egress check).

Triggers we recommend adding to the runbook (technical):
- 5-min rolling error-rate >1.5x baseline (as Vanessa suggested).
- 95th percentile latency >2x SLO for two consecutive 5-min buckets.
- KV warm start failure rate >10% after warmup timeout.
- Any critical disk or GPU allocation failures surfaced by node-level health probes.

I'll attach a short network FQDN mapping for their team to review. Also, for the version freeze manifest: we'll produce a CSV with component, pinned-tag, and SHA>256.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
